data.title: Merlin appoints Bob Smith as interim CEO
data.description:
Merlin (MRLN) announced Wednesday that its board of directors has appointed Bob Smith, a member of the Board, as chairman and interim chief executive officer, effective November 18, 2026.

The company highlighted that Smith succeeds founder Matt George, who has resigned as chief executive officer, Chairman, and a member of the board of directors and has transitioned to the role of founder and advisor. 

The firm added that Smith brings more than three decades of aerospace and defense leadership. As chief executive officer of Blue Origin from 2017 to 2024, he transitioned the company from a research organization into an operating business, growing annual sales from nearly zero to more than $750M and building an order book of approximately $10B.

Previously, he spent more than a decade at Honeywell Aerospace, including as president of Mechanical Systems and Components, a business with more than $4 billion in annual revenue, and as chief technology officer, responsible for more than 12,000 engineers and technologists.

Before Honeywell, he worked on upgrading the NASA space shuttle at United Space Alliance. He also currently serves as a senior advisor to the Office of the Secretary of Defense as part of the Business Operators for National Defense (BOND) program and as a director of Parsons Corporation.

Source: press release

data.title: Merck inks cancer research deal with AI drug discovery firm Isomorphic Labs
data.description:
Merck (MRK) is joining hands with AI-driven drug discovery firm Isomorphic Labs to discover drug candidates against cancer, the companies announced on Thursday.

As part of the collaboration, Isomorphic Labs will leverage its drug design engine (IsoDDE) and data sets supplied by Merck (MRK) to discover small molecules against an undisclosed oncology target.

The pharma giant will be responsible for their preclinical and clinical studies, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of the treatments resulting from the deal.

Per the terms, Isomorphic Labs will be eligible for an upfront payment and subsequent payments tied to R&D, regulatory, and commercial milestones.

The London-headquartered firm will also receive tiered royalties based on net sales of commercialized products and an option that allows it to earn higher royalties if it joins Merck (MRK) to fund their development activities.

data.title: GlobalFoundries in spotlight as Wedbush sees humanoid trialing as positive step
data.description:
• GlobalFoundries (GFS) was in the spotlight on Thursday as Wedbush Securities said the company trialing Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid is a positive step for the semiconductor foundry.
  • “While near-term financial impact is likely immaterial, we see the partnership as consistent with GF’s push toward automation and predictive maintenance to improve utilization and cost competitiveness, particularly at its higher-cost US and European sites,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “Longer term, robotics adoption is also a potential demand driver for the power, sensing, and connectivity chips that sit squarely in GF’s specialty portfolio.”
  • Media reports have indicated that Boston Dynamics will begin field testing Atlas at a key GlobalFoundries site early next year. That would make GlobalFoundries the first customer for Atlas outside the automotive industry. 
  • GlobalFoundries is also expanding its use of Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot, which has been used at its Vermont fab for more than four years, to its New York, Dresden, and Singapore locations.

data.title: Marsh's Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse, terms undisclosed
data.description:
Marsh's (MRSH) management consulting business, Oliver Wyman, is set to acquire technology consulting and AI platform company Synpulse.

Synpulse serves banks, insurers, wealth managers, and other financial services organizations. 

Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027.

data.title: Wall Street banks reap $550M of fees from Anthropic's blockbuster IPO
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) is paying $550M in fees to the Wall Street banks underwriting its record $107.3B IPO, according to a filing, exceeding the $500M in underwriter fees for SpaceX's (SPCX) debut offering.

Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) are leading the offering, with 20 other banks also listed in the prospectus for 980M shares being offered. Like the SpaceX (SPCX) IPO, Anthropic (ANT) also took the unusual step of not paying fees for the so-called overallotment, also known as a greenshoe. If the shares weaken in early trading, banks can support the stock by employing the over-allotment shares.

IPOs, on average, raise less than $1B per offering. Investment banks typically get 4%-7% of the size of the offering. However, that fee generally drops for larger IPOs to clinch a role in a high-profile deal.

Wall Street's biggest banks brought in the most revenue from advising on equity offerings in Q2 2026 since 2021, in large part because of the SpaceX debut, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Goldman (GS) led the ranking for the quarter ended Sept. 30, it said.

Other banks holding significant roles in the Anthropic (ANT) IPO are J.P. Morgan (JPM), Citigroup (C), Barclays (BCS), and Wells Fargo (WFC).

data.title: Arrive AI eliminates all its outstanding debt
data.description:
• Arrive AI (ARAI) announced on Thursday that it completed a preferred equity exchange with Streeterville Capital, eliminating nearly $3.96 million in debt.
  • The payment represents all the company's outstanding debt, it added.
  • Arrive AI management believes the transaction addresses a significant financing headwind and positions Arrive AI to pursue additional capital opportunities that support commercialization and long-term shareholder value.
  • Shares of the company rose over 8% in pre-market trading.
  • Press Release

data.title: PDD shares climb as profit growth offsets revenue miss
data.description:
PDD Holdings (PDD) shares jumped about 11% higher in the premarket trading on Thursday after the Chinese e-commerce company reported stronger-than-expected adjusted earnings and operating profit for the third quarter, as lower operating expenses helped offset a revenue shortfall.

Revenue for PDD was largely unchanged from a year earlier at 108.34 billion yuan ($16.2 billion), missing the Bloomberg consensus estimate of 115.21 billion yuan. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per American depositary share were 21.04 yuan, beating the 18.54 yuan estimate. Diluted earnings per ADS were 20.04 yuan, also above the 17.62 yuan forecast.

Non-GAAP operating profit rose to 32.64 billion yuan from 27.08 billion yuan a year earlier, exceeding the 27.85 billion yuan estimate. Non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders slipped 1% to 31.02 billion yuan but topped the 27.29 billion yuan consensus.

Operating expenses fell 12% year over year to 31.9 billion yuan, well below the 38.5 billion yuan estimate. Sales and marketing expenses declined 17% to 25.3 billion yuan, compared with expectations of 31.7 billion yuan. Research and development expenses, however, increased 17% to 5.1 billion yuan, above the 4.8 billion yuan forecast.

Online marketing services and other revenue grew 12% to 59.8 billion yuan, beating the 56.3 billion yuan estimate. Transaction services revenue fell 12% to 48.5 billion yuan, below expectations of 58.9 billion yuan.

Net cash generated from operating activities declined to 43 billion yuan from 45.6 billion yuan a year earlier.

PDD (PDD) said it remained in a “strategic investment phase,” with spending focused on strengthening supply chain capabilities and supporting merchants. CEO Lei Chen said the company was adapting to an evolving trade and regulatory environment and would continue investing in its supply chain.

Despite today's gain, shares remain down by about 31.7% on a year-to-date basis, underperforming the broader index that rose about 7% during the same period.

data.title: Everpure jumps as Wedbush praises strong earnings, earnings
data.description:
Everpure (P) shares jumped more than 8% in premarket trading on Thursday as the flash storage company reported better-than-expected results and guidance, leading to praise from Wedbush Securities.

“We are reiterating our OUTPERFORM rating and maintaining our $130 price target, based on a PE multiple of ~30X applied to our FY28 EPS estimate plus net cash,” Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “The unchanged target reflects a third consecutive raise to the FY27 outlook, record [operating margins] of 23.6%, a second top-five hyperscale win that ramps in FY28, and a FQ4 guide that we believe leaves room for upside, balanced against list price reductions and uncertainty around how quickly NAND costs normalize. While this multiple sits above the recent two-year average, we would note that we believe P earnings likely move higher from here, and that P has enjoyed higher multiples during periods of accelerated growth.”

For the period ending Nov. 1, Everpure said it earned an adjusted $0.86 per share as revenue jumped 51.4% year-over-year to come in at $1.46B. Analysts had expected the company to earn an adjusted $0.78 per share on $1.33B in revenue.

Looking to the fourth-quarter, Everpure expects revenue to be between $1.5B and $1.52B, above the estimate of $1.49B. Adjusted operating income is forecast to be between $350M and $360M.

The company also upped its guidance for fiscal 2027, as it now expects sales to be between $5.2B and $5.21B, up from a previous range of $5.03B to $50.7B. Analysts had expected $5.06B in full-year revenue.

data.title: Gates Industrial to unwind Nitta JV in Asia, to acquire interests in five Asian markets
data.description:
Gates Industrial (GTES) and Nitta Corp. said Thursday they agreed to conclude their joint venture in Asia, allowing the two companies to independently pursue growth initiatives in the region.

Gates (GTES) said it agreed to take full ownership of its power transmission business across China, India, Thailand, Korea, and Singapore by acquiring Nitta's interests in each market and to sell its interest in the Japan joint venture to Nitta.

Beginning in 1986, Gates (GTES) has been a 51% owner of each of the joint venture entities, which manufacture and sell power transmission products such as belts and tensioners.

Gates (GTES) agreed to make $112M in net purchase price payments and $40.2M in dividend payments to Nitta for equity interests in connection with the closing of the transaction.

The company estimated the transaction will lower its 2027 adjusted consolidated sales by $88M-$108M and reduce its 2027 adjusted EBITDA by $26M-$32M.
